title: RevisionDojo Predicted Papers Review: Exam Accuracy
summary: An honest RevisionDojo predicted papers review covering exam similarity, difficulty concerns, evidence, limitations, and how to use them effectively.
body_markdown:
RevisionDojo predicted papers can be useful for full-paper practice, but they should not be treated as exact forecasts or as replacements for official IB specimen and past papers. The current complaint that some sets feel easier than the real exam is credible, particularly because difficulty can vary by subject, paper, and examination session.


The most defensible verdict is that RevisionDojo predicted papers are **supplementary simulations** . They can develop timing, stamina, syllabus coverage, and familiarity with markschemes, but a high score on one paper is not reliable proof that the real examination will feel equally manageable.


### RevisionDojo predicted papers review: the short verdict


RevisionDojo describes its[IB Predicted Papers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/predicted-papers) as examiner-written practice papers based on the current syllabus and patterns across previous sessions. Most include a markscheme, while some subjects also provide model answers or source booklets.


That makes them more structured than an arbitrary worksheet. However, they remain third-party practice materials rather than official IB examination papers, and the word **predicted** does not establish that the topics, question wording, difficulty curve, or grade boundaries will match the upcoming session.


Review question Honest assessment


Do they resemble IB papers? Often in broad structure, timing, command terms, and mark allocation


Do they predict exact questions? No, and students should not expect them to


Is the difficulty always realistic? No, some students report that particular sets feel easier than official papers


Can they predict a final grade? Not from one attempt, especially without verified grade boundaries


Are they still useful? Yes, when combined with official specimens, past papers, and targeted correction


### What “predicted” actually means


A predicted paper is a newly written practice examination designed around what its authors believe an upcoming assessment could reasonably contain. RevisionDojo says its papers draw on the , patterns from past sessions, common command terms, expected paper structure, and typical mark allocation.
